clue.text: Denied assistance to raise profits

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising one piece sets it above the other, so the profits come first

parts.note: profits are gains
assistance is aid

explanation.surface: Someone was refused help to boost their earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'to raise' sets the profits on top of the assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or refuse, so gainsaid is a past-tense synonym of denied.

clue.text: List that man will read out

indicators.note: read out signals that the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: contracted, the words are he'll

explanation.surface: Someone will recite a list of names.
explanation.walkthrough: HE'LL, said aloud, matches the nautical verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lists leans to one side, and the sailing verb heel means exactly that tilt.

clue.text: Contents of basket perhaps cut overhead for stocking shop

indicators.note: in a down clue the head is the top letter, which is chopped off

parts.note: a hosier sells stockings and socks, standing here for the shop

explanation.surface: A shop selling stockings trims its overheads, maybe including what is in its baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead' looks like business costs; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is a willow whose pliant twigs are woven into baskets, so it is what a basket may be made of.

clue.text: Learners collectively set watch beforehand

indicators.note: beforehand places the watching word ahead of the set word

parts.note: to study something is to watch it closely
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Students arrange to keep an eye on something in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A study group is a band of pupils who meet to learn together, so it names learners as a body.

clue.text: Lake is home to river fish

indicators.note: the lake houses the river, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A lake contains fish that live in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarpon is a large silvery game fish of warm Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Colour that woman goes around Bill

indicators.note: the woman word wraps itself about the bill word

parts.note: a woman referred to is she
a bill is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: A woman blushes as she walks round a man called Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a particular tone or hue, so it can stand for a colour.

clue.text: Dismisses report of something in the wind

indicators.note: a report is a sound, so the word heard stands in for one spelt differently

parts.note: the saxophone is a member of the wind section of a band

explanation.surface: Someone brushes off rumours that something is brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something in the wind' reads as an idiom for a brewing plot, but it is a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack staff is to fire them, so sacks means discharges from a job.

clue.text: Meagre spoils that won't get you very far

definitions.text: that won't get you very far

parts.note: meagre means short, scanty
spoils taken are a haul

explanation.surface: A thin share of loot will not take you a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-haul flights or routes cover only small distances, so they don't carry you much of a way.

clue.text: Naked young man charges for the exit?

indicators.note: stripped bare, the young man loses his outer letters

parts.note: a youth is a young man
wards are those in someone's charge

explanation.surface: A nude lad is charged and heads for the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naked' takes the ends off YOUTH, leaving the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading for the exit means moving out, away from inside, which is moving towards the outside.

clue.text: Allegiance changing sides in The King's Head?

indicators.note: right is swapped for left, the R becoming L

parts.note: the head of state as a monarch, so kingship or royalty

explanation.surface: Loyalties shift inside a pub called The King's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King's Head' looks like a pub name; it means the crown itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty is faithful devotion to a cause or ruler, a straight synonym of allegiance.

clue.text: Articulate argument against leading banker meeting another

indicators.note: leading puts the argument ahead of the other piece

parts.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons
articulate speech is fluent

explanation.surface: A well-spoken objection is raised against a top banker meeting a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Confluent describes streams that flow together, so it is a river joining a second one.

clue.text: West Indian bogeyman buttoned up pyjama trousers

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the words hold the answer

explanation.surface: A Caribbean spook wears fastened pyjama bottoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb: the phrase pockets the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Caribbean folklore a duppy is a ghost or malevolent spirit.

clue.text: Follow programme about modern times

indicators.note: the programme goes round the modern times

parts.note: a television programme is a show
AD, anno domini, marks the modern era

explanation.surface: Keep watching a series about the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to tail them closely, a synonym of follow.

clue.text: Making United advance upset other half of Manchester

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are disordered
the first half of the city's name is taken

explanation.surface: Manchester United's push forward upsets their rivals across the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles OTHER plus MANCH, the first half of Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: An army on the march is advancing, so the phrase describes a united body moving forward.

clue.text: Unimportant constituency in The Borders

definitions.meaning: a seat held by a small majority, which could easily change hands
lying at the edges or margins of something

explanation.surface: A minor parliamentary seat in the Scottish Borders region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Borders is a region of southern Scotland; here it just means edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A marginal matter is peripheral, a marginal seat is narrowly held, and marginal notes sit at a page's edges.

clue.text: It's found in allure and attraction initially

indicators.note: found in puts one piece within the other

parts.note: allure is charm
the apostrophe s is short for is

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter

explanation.surface: Something lies at the heart of allure and attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' alone is the definition, the old slang for sex appeal; the apostrophe s stands for 'is', and 'found in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' is old slang for magnetic personal appeal, which is what charisma names.

clue.text: Split the cost of work with mate

parts.note: a machine that works goes
Dutch, as in 'my old Dutch', is Cockney slang for a wife or mate

explanation.surface: Share the bill for a job done with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is London Cockney slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is the idiom for each paying their own share of a bill.

clue.text: American flapper with broken leg clutching stretcher

indicators.note: the rearranged leg holds the stretcher inside it
broken means the letters are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: the rack was a torture device that stretched its victims

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper in America breaks a leg and is carried off on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes GLE, and 'clutching' wraps it round the torture device.
explanation.definitionFit: A grackle is an American blackbird, and a flapper here is anything with wings.

clue.text: Opening 24 hours of hostilities as described by Oxford historian?

indicators.note: William Spooner, Oxford don and historian, famously swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: hostilities are war
twenty-four hours make a day

explanation.surface: A day of fighting as chronicled by an Oxford scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: WAR DAY with its first sounds swapped gives 'daw way', which in non-rhotic British speech sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is the gap or entrance that a door fills, an opening in a wall.

clue.text: Archbishop's big attraction? Looking up players' kit!

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Ebor is the signature of the Archbishop of York
a draw is something that pulls crowds

explanation.surface: An archbishop gazes up at the costumes of a theatre troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking up' turns the joined EBORDRAW round.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's wardrobe is its stock of costumes, the outfits the actors wear.

clue.text: Mature actors heartlessly teased hams

indicators.note: teased out, the letters are pulled apart and rearranged
without their middle letters only the outside pair are left

explanation.surface: Experienced performers cruelly mocked overacting players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves AS from actors; 'teased' rearranges MATURE plus AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hams are poor, overacting performers, and amateurs in the derogatory sense are unskilled ones.

clue.text: Shocked by a nameless author having a heart transplant

indicators.note: the central letter is replaced, here by the letter a

parts.note: a ghostwriter is an author whose name doesn't appear on the book

explanation.surface: Appalled by an anonymous writer undergoing cardiac surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having a heart transplant' swaps the middle O of GHOST for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or amazement, a synonym of shocked.

clue.text: Vitality seen in the most elevated of characters here

definitions.text: seen in the most elevated of characters here
definitions.meaning: in written Greek a breathing mark sits above initial vowels; characters here also hints at the puzzle's ghosts

explanation.surface: Energy is visible in the finest people around.
explanation.walkthrough: The rough and smooth breathings of Greek are marks written above letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit means vigour and liveliness, and it also names a ghost like the puzzle's other phantoms.

clue.text: Article beginning to translate Paul's second letter to the Thessalonians

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of what follows
the second letter of the name is picked

explanation.surface: A paper starting to render Paul's Second Epistle to the Thessalonians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter to the Thessalonians' is a Greek letter, Thessalonica being a Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, the script the Thessalonians used.

clue.text: Get used to guarantee not having succeeded

indicators.note: S is short for succeeded, as in genealogies, and it is dropped

parts.note: to insure is to guarantee against loss

explanation.surface: Accept that a promise has failed to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to accustom them to something unpleasant, so it means to habituate.

clue.text: Seabird's return conveys what unearthly vision to Wellington?

indicators.note: conveys means carries, so the bird holds the other piece
return means the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: the auk is a diving seabird
eh is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: A seabird coming back carries some ghostly sight to the New Zealand capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellington is New Zealand's capital, so the word is Maori.
explanation.definitionFit: In Maori belief a kehua is a ghost, so it is a phantom as a New Zealander might see one.

clue.text: Wave off five boarding gravy train

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the numeral goes inside

parts.note: a sinecure is a cushy job, a gravy train
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Waving goodbye as five people get on a lucrative train.
explanation.definitionFit: A sine curve is the smooth oscillating shape of a wave in mathematics and physics.

clue.text: Friend quietly abandons idiot

indicators.note: abandons means the quiet letter leaves

parts.note: a chump is a fool
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A pal quietly walks out on a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Chum is informal for a pal or close companion.

clue.text: Place to park rear end of university gravy train?

definitions.meaning: a chair is a professorship, so a cushy one is an undemanding academic post

explanation.surface: Where a lazy academic sits on an easy job.
explanation.walkthrough: A chair is also a university professorship.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is an armchair to sink into, and read as an easy professorship it's an academic sinecure.

clue.text: 12 like being upset and avoiding offence

indicators.note: avoiding means the reversed letters are left out

parts.note: to take umbrage is to take offence

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word for like is reversed

parts.note: eg, for example, means like

explanation.surface: Someone is upset in a similar way and keeps clear of causing offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is SHADOW. 'being upset' turns EG into GE, which is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the darkest central part of a shadow, and the word is Latin for shade.
